summary: AquaPulse is an innovative web-based platform developed by team Smansaden Horizon to monitor water resources and assess drought risks using open NASA satellite data (such as AMSR-2 and POWER). By translating complex telemetry into an interactive, user-friendly dashboard deployed on GitHub Pages, AquaPulse tackles critical water scarcity challenges. This project is essential because it provides vulnerable regions and local communities with timely, accessible insights for rapid and effective environmental mitigation.
details:
AquaPulse is an integrated web-based platform designed for water resource monitoring and drought risk assessment.


How it works & Functions:
It leverages NASA open data APIs (such as AMSR-2 and POWER) to track water availability, soil moisture, and meteorological indicators, presenting actionable insights through an interactive web dashboard.


Benefits & Expected Impact:
The platform empowers vulnerable regions and local communities with timely data to mitigate water scarcity, optimize clean water management, and build long-term environmental resilience.


Tools & Technologies:
Developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and hosted publicly via GitHub Pages for seamless accessibility and fast performance.


Creativity & Considerations:
AquaPulse translates complex satellite telemetry into an intuitive, lightweight, and user-friendly interface, focusing on accessibility, speed, and practical local usability for rapid decision-making.
